verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Bhavnagar re-rollers with own scrap linkages and branded TMT offtake; avoid traders and single-mill converters until scrap supply and realisation are verified.
title: Bhavnagar steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Bhavnagar re-roller buys scrap, melts or heats it, rolls billets into TMT bars and sells to builders, dealers and government contractors. **Cash is made on the spread between scrap cost and TMT realisation, not on volume alone.** The local signal is stark: scrap prices are rising while ship-breaking supply at Alang is at the bottom [1]. Alang is the town's scrap artery, so when ship arrivals fall, the mill pays more for input and margins compress before sales even slow. **So when a proposal lands, check the mill's scrap sourcing mix; if it depends mainly on Alang ship scrap, ask what alternate billet or sponge supply it has tied up.**

## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in brand and dealer network, not in the furnace. Captain Steel built a TMT brand with celebrity endorsement and commands a premium over market rates [7] — that is the model to back. Working capital is the real risk: peers carry moderately high working-capital needs supported by bank lines [9], and gearing at one peer deteriorated to 1.80x as on March 31, 2024 from 1.40x a year earlier on debt-funded acquisition and higher working-capital borrowings [8]. **So size the limit to the operating cycle, not to the fixed asset; if drawing power is routinely fully used, ask for the month-wise stock-and-debtor statement before renewal.**

## What has changed now
National steel demand is holding: IIP for NIC 24 output rose 2.4% YoY and 3.4% Apr-to-date [D]. Gujarat is running ahead of India on GST collections, +11.9% versus +6.1% [D], and electricity demand +11.0% versus +9.5% [D] — a real local tailwind. Peer results confirm volume pull: Steel Exchange India clocked ~₹340 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, up ~45% YoY [4], and Rathi Steel crossed ₹200 crore with ~28.86% volume growth [5]. **But the Alang scrap squeeze [1] is the offsetting fact; treat rising input cost against firm demand as a margin test, not a growth signal.** Note the rating reports are old — ICRA March 2024 [6] and February 2023 [7] — so use them for structure, not current numbers.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
Pursue integrated or partly integrated re-rollers with own billet or sponge capacity, branded TMT with dealer pull, and mills selling into Gujarat government and housing demand. Avoid pure scrap traders, single-furnace converters with no brand, and borrowers whose sales are to one or two dealers. **Structure: cash-flow-backed limits, monthly stock-and-debtor statements, and a covenant that gearing stays below the level at sanction.** Take every month: scrap purchase invoices, TMT sales register, electricity bills (a proxy for running hours), and GST returns. **If GST turnover trails bank credits, ask for the sales register and dealer confirmations.**

## Early-warning signs
- Alang ship arrivals and local scrap price (weekly): if scrap rises while TMT realisation is flat, cut limit utilisation and re-price.
- Electricity consumption versus rated capacity (monthly): a fall below normal running hours means the mill is idling — ask why before renewal.
- Debtor days and dealer concentration (monthly): if top-two dealers cross half of sales, seek diversification or reduce exposure.
- Gearing and interest coverage (quarterly): if gearing crosses the sanction level, freeze fresh disbursement.
- GST return versus bank statement (monthly): a persistent gap means off-book sales or diversion — escalate.
